title: Fine tune 20 Llama Models in 5 Minutes: Santosh Radha
talk_summary: A five-minute demo of Covalent, an open-source Python framework that lets you decorate plain Python functions with compute requirements (GPU type, memory, time limit) and ship them to local or cloud backends without Docker/Kubernetes. The example loops over many models, fine-tunes each on an H100, evaluates on cheaper L4/V100 machines, sorts results on CPU, and deploys the best—all from a notebook.

takeaways.what_they_do: Each Python function declares its own hardware (CPU cores, GPU type, memory, max runtime) and the orchestrator routes it to a matching backend, so cheap steps don't burn GPUs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I want this to run on a CPU based machion I don't want to waste GPU for my sorting
takeaways.numbers: evaluation on L4: 6 min, $0.87; another model on V100: 6 min, $0.11

takeaways.what_they_do: A single workflow loops over N models, calls fine-tune then evaluate per model, collects accuracies, sorts, and deploys the winner—expressed as ordinary Python rather than a DSL.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Simply Loop over a bunch of models to finetune call the fine tune function evaluate the task and get the accuracy

takeaways.technique: Pay-per-second ephemeral compute for batch jobs
takeaways.what_they_do: Jobs run only for their actual duration on rented GPUs and return a Python object; no persistent cluster.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it runs for 5 minutes you pay for 5 minutes of h00 it runs for 10 seconds you pay for 10 seconds
